Svelte Integration with

integrates with Svelte through . The package preserves the core contract and makes the existing state Snapshot getter reactive within Svelte effects.

Svelte package usage

can run in a Svelte application without . The core APIs remain available, but the Svelte-reactive State getter is supplied only by the Svelte package.

Svelte version requirement

requires Svelte 5.7 or a later Svelte 5 release. The reactive State getter uses createSubscriber(), which became available in Svelte 5.7.

Svelte Integration

is a Svelte integration wrapper around the core APIs. It preserves the core FluentApi, synchronous State Snapshot, and State Stream while making the existing state getter the Svelte reactive State surface.

Read state through $derived, $effect, or template rendering. The Svelte effect lifecycle owns the resulting subscription and exposes subsequent State changes through the same Snapshot getter, so the component does not require a separate state$ subscription or manual subscription cleanup.

Initial State requires a reactive connection

A manual state$ subscription created after the has initialized can miss the emission that committed the initial State. Later State updates may still reach that subscription even though the component did not receive the current Snapshot during its initial evaluation.

Reading state within Svelte reactivity gives the component the current Snapshot and connects it to subsequent State changes through the same effect lifecycle. Outside Svelte reactivity, read state for the latest synchronous Snapshot or use state$ when an explicitly managed Observable subscription is required.

Installation

The Svelte extension is available from the package on npm. 

{{`npm install @sdux-vault/svelte`}}

Svelte Component Pattern

Create and initialize the outside the component, then import its stable reference into the Svelte component. Read state through $derived and render from the resulting reactive Snapshot. 

{{`import { FeatureCell, Vault } from '@sdux-vault/svelte';

Vault({
  logLevel: 'off',
  devMode: false
});

export const counterCell = FeatureCell<number>({
  key: 'counter',
  initialState: 0
});

counterCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`<script lang="ts">
import { counterCell } from './counter.cell';

let snapshot = $derived(counterCell.state);
</script>

{#if snapshot.isLoading}
  <p>Loading...</p>
{:else if snapshot.error}
  <p role="alert">{snapshot.error.message}</p>
{:else if !snapshot.hasValue}
  <p>No State is available.</p>
{:else}
  <p>Count: {snapshot.value}</p>
{/if}`}}
Reactive State getter

Reading state within Svelte reactivity connects the current effect to State and returns the latest committed immutable Snapshot. Its value, hasValue, isLoading, and error fields represent the State available to the current effect.
